_comment: Where ScreenTail looks for updates and whose signature it accepts on an update manifest (ST-113, ADR-0008).
Compiled into the client (ScreenTail.Core embeds this file) and read by installer/update-manifest.ps1,
which checks every manifest it signs against these keys before CI uploads it. Nothing here is a secret:
the keys are public keys, and the private key lives in Azure Key Vault and never leaves it.
feed: the HTTPS folder the manifests are served from, ending in a slash. The client asks for
<feed><channel>/win-x64.json and sends nothing else: no device, no tenant, no version, no cookie.
packageHosts: the exact host names a manifest's package URL may name. No wildcards.
keys: ECDSA P-256 public keys, as base64 DER SubjectPublicKeyInfo, each with the id a manifest names.
Empty until the owner creates the signing key and the hosting (docs/dev/installer.md, 'Updates').
Until then a build does not check for updates at all and says so in Settings: it fails closed.
Rotating the key: add the new key here, ship a release signed by the old key that carries both,
then sign with the new one; remove the old key a release later.
